To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most accurate and robust technique is the 8-point algorithm, followed by the 7-point algorithm and the LMedS algorithm.

the fundamental matrix is the most robust measure of epipolar geometry; the most robust method for estimating it is the 8-point algorithm; and its most robust estimate is obtained by using RANSAC to select the best 8-point algorithm estimate.
the 5-point algorithm is the best method for estimating the fundamental and the essential matrices; the 8-point algorithm and the 7-point algorithm are the second best; the LMedS method is the worst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of epipolar geometry and its uncertainty from two uncalibrated views.
the estimation of epipolar geometry and its uncertainty from two images.
two aspects of the epipolar problem: 1) the development of new techniques for determining the fundamental matrix and 2) the evaluation of these techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method of eight point algorithm and the RANSAC algorithm are the most efficient methods in terms of accuracy and computational cost.

the most reliable and accurate method is to estimate the essential matrix from the essential constraints, and the least reliable and accurate method would be to compute the fundamental matrix from the eight-point algorithm.
the method of RANSAC is the best one to estimate the fundamental matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method, which can estimate the fundamental matrix and the epipolar uncertainty in a unified framework, and we have compared it with other methods.
we have provided the most complete review on the topic of epipolar geometry and its uncertainty.
the most reliable techniques to estimate the epipolar constraint are those based on the 8- and 11-point algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the fundamental matrix can be determined very accurately from point correspondences, the uncertainty in the fundamental matrix is very difficult to determine.
there is a need for a more robust and efficient method of determining the epipolar uncertainty.
, in general, there is no single method which outperforms the others.
